questions.question: How wide should BUG-280's fix go on LocalBackend?

options.label: Three scans + recursive (Recommended)
options.description: Map PermissionError → PermissionDenied in list_files (all three branches: iterdir, rglob, os.walk), list_folders, iter_children. Recursive walks raise on a denied subtree instead of silently dropping it, matching SFTP. User-visible: a partially unreadable tree now raises mid-iteration where it used to return a short listing. glob's same silent drop gets filed as a follow-up.

options.label: Three scans + recursive + glob
options.description: As above, and glob() also raises PermissionDenied on a denied subtree. Wider behaviour change in one PR; glob's contract for denied subtrees isn't stated in the spec yet, so this also needs a spec sentence.

options.label: Literal item only
options.description: Fix only the non-recursive iterdir scans in the three methods. Smallest diff, but leaves list_files(denied) raising while list_files(denied, recursive=True) returns []: an inconsistency the fix itself creates. Recursive silent drop filed separately.

questions.question: The item's open decision: fix here, or fix the listing-generator pattern once across backends?

options.label: Fix here only (Recommended)
options.description: Patch LocalBackend's listings. S3Boto3 (BUG-249) and SFTP (BUG-146) are already fixed, so Local is the remaining known instance. The 'once across backends' mechanism is RFC-0017's contract kernel, which already cites BUG-280 as motivation. Record that pointer in the close.

options.label: Shared base helper now
options.description: Add a listing-error wrapper in the Backend base and route Local through it. That pre-empts RFC-0017's design in a bug-fix PR, and the existing S3/SFTP fixes would stay as they are anyway.

questions.question: Round 1 confirmed that `Store.get_folder_info` now answers differently by `max_depth`: `max_depth=N` raises PermissionDenied (through list_files), and `max_depth=None` returns an under-count (LocalBackend.get_folder_info still uses rglob). How should this PR handle it?

options.description: LocalBackend.get_folder_info walks with the same os.walk + _raise_if_denied hook and maps PermissionError → PermissionDenied; adds a Raises: line, test cells, and a migration-guide sentence. Both max_depth forms then agree. glob stays filed as BUG-311.

options.label: Fold into BUG-311
options.description: Widen BUG-311 to 'glob and get_folder_info drop a denied subtree'. This PR then ships the max_depth split, documented as a known gap in the migration guide.

options.label: File a separate item
options.description: New BUG item for get_folder_info alone. This PR ships the split, documented as a known gap.

questions.question: Round 3 confirmed a gap in the guarantee this PR states. On Python 3.14 (POSIX), `Path.is_file()` returns False when a child can't be stat'ed, so a folder that is listable but not traversable (e.g. mode 0o444) silently drops its files from list_files/get_folder_info. Separately, the `is_file()`→`stat()` pair leaks a raw FileNotFoundError if a file vanishes in between. How should the PR handle these?

options.label: Fix in this PR (Recommended)
options.description: Replace each walk's is_file()+stat() with one stat per child: PermissionError propagates (→ PermissionDenied), FileNotFoundError means 'vanished, skip', S_ISREG decides file. Closes both gaps and makes the stated guarantee true on 3.11–3.14. Test cells deny os.stat on children, portable to Windows. Folder classification (is_dir in list_folders/iter_children) gets the same treatment.

options.label: Narrow claims and file
options.description: Reword the docstrings/test docstring to 'a folder the OS refuses to list' and say a child that can't be stat'ed is not covered; file one new BUG item for both gaps. Smaller diff; the 3.14 silent drop ships.

On Python 3.14 (POSIX), `Path.is_file()` returns False when a child can't be stat'ed, so a folder that is listable but not traversable (e.g. mode 0o444) silently drops its files from list_files/get_folder_info. The round-3 sibling sweep found `LocalBackend.get_file_info` has the same defect outside this PR's methods: it classifies with `is_dir()`/`is_file()`, so a file whose parent can't be traversed answers `NotFound` on 3.14 (POSIX) and leaks a raw `PermissionError` on 3.11–3.13, where BE-021 wants `PermissionDenied`. Read from code, not run. How should it be tracked?
